title: Debt and Safehouse
premise: Cyrus Ravensworth has spent years laundering reputations, not money—scrubbing scandals for the powerful while keeping her own name off every ledger. When a burner phone rings with the voice of her presumed-dead mentor, Elias Voss, she learns he faked his death to expose a laundering network that now plans to trigger a 'market accident' in Frankfurt at opening bell. Pursued by both the network and her own agency, which wants her silent, Cyrus must choose between protecting her found family of misfit analysts and finishing what Elias started. She stops the attack by turning the network's own clean-money trail against it, but at the cost of exposing herself—and choosing love over the duty that made her invisible.
about_author: Freya Fairweather is a former compliance analyst who traded spreadsheets for suspense after a decade watching fortunes quietly change hands. She writes thrillers about the people who keep secrets for a living, from a farmhouse office with terrible phone reception.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A routine scrub job for a shipping magnate is interrupted when an unregistered burner rings: Elias Voss, dead two years, alive on the line, warning of something scheduled in Frankfurt. When she traces the call, her safehouse is compromised. The emotional beat is dread—the comfortable invisibility she built begins collapsing in a single night.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Cyrus and her analyst team—her found family of exiles and burnouts—as they follow Voss's cryptic clues through shell companies toward a Frankfurt clearing house. Her agency handler, Marlowe, orders her to stand down; she realizes the network has friends inside. The beat is loyalty tested: trust the institution or the ghost.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, racing to Frankfurt. She confronts Voss face to face, learns he used her as the network's unwitting architect, and that the 'accident' is a derivatives cascade timed to the open. With minutes left, she and her team inject a poisoned trade into the cascade. The climax is betrayal and sacrifice colliding as the markets tick toward catastrophe.

chapters.title: What We Owe
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, aftermath. The cascade fails; the network unravels publicly, but Voss vanishes again and Marlowe offers her erasure in exchange for silence. Instead, Cyrus testifies, burning her anonymity to protect her team—the found family that stayed. The resolution lands on love against duty: she chooses to be seen, and survives it.
